recommendation: HYBRID: "THE LIMB HAND-OFF" â€” repurpose's limb geometry + mask (steps 1-7) as the falling element, carried by replace's scheduling fixes (steps 4,5,6) as the rising element, with a SAFER ch6 gate width (0.16, not 0.175). Reject "minimal" outright (its model class is wrong at the decisive step). Reject "replace"'s bank deletion and its pre-boundary spaceReveal (breaks an ordering invariant and the owner's goal). Take from "minimal" only its diagnosis, not its edits.
rationale:
I scored the BANKOFF control arm myself: with the bank off EVERY descent step already passes (worst -28.5/0.01p); the run fails on a +96.2/0.01p pop at p=0.7441 where spaceReveal binary-flips ch6 on, plus tail rises at 0.7941/0.8001. So the bank is patching a SCHEDULING hole, not a painting hole â€” and it patches it by being a 100%-opaque wall that HIDES that pop. Any fix that makes the bank transparent exposes it.

That kills "minimal". It models the bank as additive over a fixed background, but the bank is an occluder (opacity is a hard-clamped 1.0 at both 0.7401 and 0.7441 â€” I verified the density arithmetic: t=0.5333, d=0.9333, clamp(0.9333^2*1.25)=1.0). Under the correct model L = A*L_bank + (1-A)*B, its own near-fade to mean alpha 0.72 leaks 28% of the +38.5 pop = +29/0.01p, a post-boundary rise it never predicted and its step 8 cannot touch. It is 2-of-4 gates, not 3. Its geometry is also unfit: at p=0.7501 the eye is 6.2 u from the shell centre with the FBM frozen on an object-space shell â€” zero parallax, so you never "go past" anything.

I refuted "replace" on a guard it did not audit: completing spaceReveal AT the boundary breaks `expect(ch6).toBeLessThan(gateEnd)` (odyssey-seam-56-schedule.test.js:101), an ORDERING invariant, not a tunable number. It also puts a black hole and accretion disk in a blue daylight sky (contradicting cosmic-expanse.js:717-722), touches 10 materials across 2 files with zero test coverage, and deleting the bank forfeits owner goal #3 â€” "go past the fluffy clouds out in space" requires clouds to be gone past.

"repurpose" is the only design whose mechanism survives measurement, and its self-negation is honest: I confirmed the camera is pitched +15Â° to +36Â° through the whole window with only 0-29% of frame below the horizon, so the "receding floor" reading is dead and the limb band (26-58% binary coverage, weighted less) is the only in-frame instrument. I also confirmed its enabling geometric claim: at r=620 the camera is inside the ellipsoid at every station (e=0.025-0.515), INCLUDING p=0.7941/0.8001 where today's r=150 shell is outside (e=1.112/1.236) and where I measured L_on == L_off exactly (16.28/16.31, 18.87/18.91) â€” the bank contributes literally zero there today. That is the limb's unique, non-duplicated value.

But repurpose is not sufficient alone, and I proved it numerically. I modelled the widened gate against the real background: even at spaceGateBand 0.16 the post-boundary steps are still +14.3, +17.3, +8.5, +6.6 and +4.3 per 0.01p â€” FIVE rises. Space arriving after the boundary is a rise BY CONSTRUCTION unless something luminous is simultaneously falling. So the design must be a HAND-OFF: a falling limb (repurpose) plus a rising cosmos whose arrival is spread (widened gate) AND whose late tail is fixed at source. Solving the tail constraint exactly reproduces repurpose's own numbers (K(0.7861) >= 3.66, K(0.7941) >= 0.80) â€” but those land inside the metric's ~1.7/0.01p capture noise, so the tail must NOT be masked by the limb. It must be removed at source, which is precisely replace's step 6 / minimal's step 8 (void dome + nebula field are camera-y `nebulaReveal` driven and still climbing past the window). Both designs converged there independently; that is the strongest signal in the whole set and it is mandatory.

I import replace's step 5 (sky recedes into the never-sampled `edge-of-space` keyframe) because I verified scriptP = 0.05 + progress*0.9 caps at 0.95 and the p=1.00 keyframe with skyHorizon 0x1b3f79 has NEVER been sampled â€” a fully authored asset lying idle. It is worth +14.2 luma at p=0.7101 and +13.4 at 0.7161, exactly where my measured background collapses (44.2 -> 15.7 -> 4.7 -> 1.8). It is complementary to the limb, not duplicative: it fades out by p=0.7221 where the limb takes over. It also directly serves owner goal #3 â€” a real deep-blue-to-vacuum gradient instead of a flat 0x05060f constant.

Modelled hybrid curve (occlusion model anchored on BOTH real captures): 82, 74, 60, 48, 48, 42, 42, 39, 34, 34, 35, 33, 31, 24, 15, 15, 17, 19. maxStep ~-17 to -25/0.01p (limit 45), tailShare ~30% (limit 50%), endLuma 18.9 (limit 60), postBoundary 0 once the tail is fixed at source. Passes all four with real margin rather than by a hair.

On the owner's words: the hybrid gives lit sculpted cumulus silhouetted against a lit limb that RECEDES from 682 u to 510 u as you climb (genuine parallax â€” you are going past them), stars and the gas giant readable in the clear 40-55% of frame above the limb, and an authored sky gradient. That is "past the fluffy clouds out in space". A smooth fade to black is what "replace" delivers and what the owner explicitly rejected.

scores.verdict: REJECT â€” right diagnosis, wrong model class, unfit geometry. Its two findings are valuable; its two edits are not the fix.
strengths: Correctly identifies the mechanism: the camera is INSIDE a BackSide shell whose opacity is a hard-clamped 1.0 at the boundary. I verified the arithmetic independently (t=0.5333 at p=0.7441, d=0.9333, clamp(0.9333^2*1.25)=1.0).

Correctly identifies that the bank's entry tone bypasses toOutput()'s departure fade â€” it paints raw cloudTop (linear luma 1.023) at the exact frame the world it belongs to has faded 100% to 0x05060f.
Correctly and verifiably proves the two tail rises at p=0.7941/0.8001 are NOT the bank's. I confirmed L_on == L_off to three digits at both stations (16.28/16.31, 18.87/18.91).
Smallest diff of the three, trips no automated guard, fully reversible.
Honest about its own residual failure and about the +/-15 luma error bar on its model.
fatalFlaws: THE MODEL CLASS IS WRONG AT THE DECISIVE STEP. It treats the bank as additive over the background; the bank is an occluder. Its predicted 0.7401->0.7441 step of +0.2 luma is impossible: with mean alpha ~0.72 the background term goes 0.74 -> 12.3, i.e. +11.6 raw = +29/0.01p, a post-boundary rise. It is 2-of-4 gates, not the 3-of-4 it claims.

The near-fade cannot separate 'overhead' from 'below' â€” it is an eye-DISTANCE mask standing in for an eye-ELEVATION mask. The correlation only holds because of the Y-squash and the eye's position, and it inverts as the eye traverses: at p=0.7501 the eye is 6.2 u from the centre so nearly every fragment is 'near' and alpha collapses everywhere, not just overhead.

At r=150 with the FBM sampled on a fixed object-space shell (positionLocal always |p|=150), the noise is frozen while the eye moves through it. There is no parallax and no sense of passing anything â€” it dissolves around you. This fails owner goal #3 even if it passed the metric.
Its step 8 (void dome re-gate) does not touch the 0.7441 pop, so its own named path to a green gate does not reach its own largest unmodelled failure.

scores.verdict: REJECT AS A WHOLE, HARVEST THREE PARTS. The best measurement work of the three and the correct root-cause framing, attached to a deletion that forfeits the owner's goal.
strengths: The single most valuable act in the set: it scored the bank-off control arm and discovered the seam is a SCHEDULING hole, not a painting hole. I reproduced this exactly â€” bank-off, every descent step passes; the failures are +96.2 at 0.7441 and the two tail rises.
Correctly proves painting alone cannot work: the camera is pitched up behind a 33 deg half-FOV, so the frame is mostly upper sky. My own ray integration confirms 0-29% of frame below horizon.

Found a genuinely unused authored asset: scriptP = 0.05 + progress*0.9 caps at 0.95, so the p=1.00 `edge-of-space` keyframe has never been sampled. I verified this in the source. Its +14.2/+13.4 luma at p=0.7101/0.7161 lands exactly on the deepest part of the measured collapse.

Correctly diagnoses the tail rises as camera-y `nebulaReveal` still climbing past the window, and proposes the right fix shape (max() with a global-progress ramp, precedent at cosmic-expanse.js:1667).
The forceSinglePass items are free and correct: aurora bridge 6 draws -> 3, streak motes 2 -> 1, with the precedent and rationale already shipped at odyssey-planet-aurora.js:301-309.
fatalFlaws: BREAKS AN ORDERING INVARIANT IT NEVER AUDITED. Completing spaceReveal AT the boundary makes gateEnd == ch6, failing `expect(ch6).toBeLessThan(gateEnd)` (odyssey-seam-56-schedule.test.js:101) and `expect(worldOff).toBeGreaterThan(gateEnd)` (:86). Its guard list names only :66 and :70. Repurpose flagged these as ordering assertions; replace walked into them.

FORFEITS THE OWNER'S GOAL. Deleting the bank means there are no clouds to go past. The owner said 'go past the fluffy clouds out in space' and explicitly rejected a smooth fade to black. This design's own predicted curve is a monotone descent to black â€” metric-green, brief-red.

Puts a black hole and accretion disk in a blue daylight sky from p~0.672, contradicting the authored decision at cosmic-expanse.js:717-722. It admits this and calls it owner-gated, but it is load-bearing for its metric, not optional.

Largest new surface by far: ten opacityNode re-arms across two files, with its own risk note conceding a missed one keeps its pop and a mis-wired one makes an element invisible for all of chapter 6, and no unit test catches either.

Its make-or-break number (Cfull on the approach, assumed flat at 41.5) is unmeasured, and it concedes that at Cfull=35 the run fails postBoundary. My own attempt to decompose it gave C(0.7441)=68.9 against C(0.7501)=35.9 â€” an implausible discontinuity that says the assumption is not yet safe.

scores.verdict: ADOPT AS THE SPINE. The only design whose mechanism survives adversarial measurement, and the only one honest enough to negate half its own brief.
strengths: Negates its own assigned angle on measurement rather than defending it. I independently confirmed the kill: camera pitched +15 to +36 deg, only 0-29% of frame below horizon, so a floor/veil below the rail cannot carry the frame.

Its enabling geometric claim is correct and I verified it: at r=620 the camera is inside the ellipsoid at every one of the 18 stations (e=0.025-0.515), including p=0.7941/0.8001 where today's r=150 shell is OUTSIDE (e=1.112/1.236) and contributes exactly zero. That tail coverage is its unique value.

Correctly identifies that the elevation mask is exact: with the eye inside a BackSide shell every screen pixel maps 1:1 to one fragment, so viewDir.y IS sin(view elevation). This is a direct control on 'sky above, cloud at the horizon', not a proxy.
Names the co-design honestly and predicts its own failure without the paired change (~+90/0.01p) rather than claiming a solo win.
Solves the tail constraint correctly â€” I re-derived K(0.7861) >= 3.66 and K(0.7941) >= 0.80 independently and got the same numbers â€” and correctly flags that they sit inside capture noise.

Cheapest guard footprint of any design that actually works: the material-contract test compares to EXPORTED constants, so radius 150 -> 620 leaves the suite green. I confirmed this by reading the test.

Spends the luma budget on ~1/3 of the frame at 3x brightness instead of 100% at 1x â€” the argument that this reads as an image rather than as fog is both the artistic and the numeric case, and they agree.
fatalFlaws: Its tail fix masks the 0.7941/0.8001 rises with a residual limb instead of removing them at source. My model reproduces its constraint but shows the resulting margin is <0.3 luma/0.01p against ~1.25-1.7 of capture noise â€” not shippable as the primary mechanism. The source fix (void dome + nebula field off global progress) is required and it does not include one.
spaceGateBand 0.175 leaves only 0.0006 of p of headroom under the hard worldOff ceiling of 0.7623. Correct arithmetic, imprudent margin. 0.16 gives 0.0025 and costs almost nothing in smoothness.
uLimbGain = 0.42 is a one-point power fit through ACES plus the output grade, and it says so. Two capture iterations are budgeted but the first capture will land visibly off.

Widening spaceGateBand delays every ch6 system together, and its tail model treats ch6's contribution as one scalar times an observed curve. The 0.7441-0.7561 rows are the least trustworthy in its table â€” and my own decomposition attempt at 0.7441 confirms that station is anomalous.

Keeps relying on toBridge for luminance travel; minimal's finding that BANK_BRIDGE is 53:1 against the entry tone means the exit residue collapse is still latent in the colour ramp if uLimbGain is set too high.

ownerDecisions: ART PREMISE, the one that gates everything: odyssey-cloud-bank.js:7-8 states 'an occlusion moment must actually occlude, and only a volume the camera is INSIDE can do that'. Under this plan the camera is still inside the shell, but the shell occludes only the horizon band (roughly the lower 45-55% of frame) and leaves the sky above clear for stars, the gas giant and the void dome. That is the correct read for a camera that now exits ABOVE the weather, and it is the only way to stop the fill without moving the mesh off the rail â€” but it is an authored premise being deliberately bent. Needs a nod, not a code change.

May chapter 6's deep-space content (stars, black hole, accretion disk, nebula) fade in across p=0.7401..0.7598 instead of 0.7401..0.7475? This is milder than replace's version â€” everything still arrives strictly AFTER the boundary, so the authored rule at cosmic-expanse.js:717-722 ('nothing but the earth may bleed into the daylight frame') is technically preserved â€” but the arrival becomes a visible 0.02-wide ramp rather than a blink. The metric cannot be passed without spreading it somehow.

Is it acceptable for the world's sky dome to hold a 1.6-2.1 luma vacuum-blue floor (the authored edge-of-space gradient) from p=0.7401 to 0.7623 instead of being crushed to literal black by the 0x05060f constant? It is invisible under chapter 6's dome, but it creates a new dependency on ch6's transparent dome sorting after the world's opaque one (currently true only because opaque draws before transparent regardless of renderOrder â€” both are -100).
